models.title: Short interest days to cover
models.summary: The owner defines short interest ratio as short interest divided by average daily share volume, expressed in days.

relationship.original_equation: Days to cover = shares sold short / average shares traded per day
relationship.locator: Data Fields and Definitions, Days to Cover, printed p2
relationship.translation_notes: Shares divided by shares per trading day gives trading-day duration; the custom share-per-day unit and trading-day context need registry review.

variables.definition: Number of reported shares held short for the security as of the selected reporting date
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Average shares traded per trading day over the stated measurement window
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Unrounded short interest divided by average daily trading volume
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Short shares and trading volume refer to the same security and use consistent split adjustments.
Average daily share volume is positive and its measurement window and trading-day convention are disclosed.
limitations: This is an approximation using recent average total volume, not a prediction of how quickly short positions can actually be closed.
Nasdaq’s cited report rounds to hundredths and displays a one-day floor for ratios at or below one; this model returns the unrounded mathematical ratio.
Short-interest data are periodic and can be stale; the result does not imply every trade is available for covering.
